original_title: Webb shows how supernova dust chronicles star evolution
abstract: Using the James Webb Space Telescope's MIRI instrument, a team led by Tea Temim examined infrared spectra of dust in the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A. The researchers distinguished regions dominated by silica dust and by carbon dust in shocked ejecta. The Green Monster, formed from material the star shed before the explosion, instead showed complex magnesium silicates. Combining these observations with X-ray data, the authors found chemical patterns consistent with mixing of burning layers inside the original star shortly before core collapse, possibly only hours before it exploded. The timing is an interpretation of the observations. The study appeared in The Astrophysical Journal Letters (DOI 10.3847/2041-8213/aea901).
